title: Regional restart summary and customer actionables (EU cluster) - 2027-07-03
content:
Audience: Customers with active traffic in EU regions and account teams (CS/AM).
Purpose: Draft text for status page updates and a concise post-incident customer summary with recommended next steps. This is a working draft — please leave comments inline.

Executive summary (one sentence):
On 2027-07-03 (UTC) an automated rolling restart of the EU inference pool triggered an unexpected session reconciliation bug which caused transient request failures and elevated error rates for ~45 minutes; most customer traffic degraded to errors or timeouts while failover policies were gradually applied.

Suggested short status-page message (for immediate posting, <2 sentences):
We experienced degraded inference availability in our EU region on 2027-07-03 due to an automated cluster restart that impacted session state reconciliation. Services have been restored and we continue to monitor; full details and customer action items are below.

Impact (customer-friendly bullets):
- Scope: Affected requests routed to eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 regions only; hosted API customers and Dedicated pools in those regions were impacted.
- Severity: Increased 5xx errors and request timeouts, affecting request throughput for roughly 45 minutes (2027-07-03 09:12–09:57 UTC).
- Surface area: Text generation, chat sessions with warmed KV caches, and streaming responses were most affected. Embeddings endpoints saw intermittent latency spikes but lower error rates.
- Data integrity: No model weights or customer data were altered; we did not observe persisted data loss.

Concise timeline (UTC):
- 09:10 — Scheduled rolling restart of EU pool (automated maintenance window) began.
- 09:12 — Monitoring alert: error rate spike on inference-service-eu-west.
- 09:14 — PagerDuty triggered; SRE investigating. Noted failed session reconciliation when nodes rejoined the mesh.
- 09:20 — Partial routing fallback to regional spare capacity started; some requests still hit nodes with stale KV session pointers.
- 09:28 — Engineering deployed a hotfix to the session-reconcile service (PR #3124), which prevents reuse of stale KV pointers during node rejoin.
- 09:40 — Automatic fallback policy adjusted to prefer cross-region failover for sensitive routes.
- 09:57 — Error rates returned to baseline for most customers; continuous monitoring kept in place.
- 12:00 — Post-incident safety checks completed; confirmed no customer-request queues held beyond normal retention window.

Root cause (plain language):
A race in the node rejoin path allowed in-memory session pointers (KV cache references) to be considered valid before the node finished flushing transient session metadata. When the scheduler routed requests to these rejoined nodes, the runtime attempted to use outdated KV pointers resulting in mismatched KV lookups and runtime failures for active chat/generation sessions. The root cause is a combination of (1) a timing regression introduced in the recent node-rejoin refactor, and (2) the rolling restart hitting a higher-than-expected concurrency of session handoffs.

Immediate mitigations applied (what we did during incident):
- Rolled out a hotfix to the reconcile worker to add a short grace-period during which KV pointers are ignored until full flush completed (PR #3124).
- Tuned routing to prefer healthy nodes in other regions for routes where latency SLOs permit cross-region failover.
- Increased observability around session state transitions and added temporary alert thresholds specific to post-restart windows.
- Manually drained and validated a subset of rejoined nodes to ensure safe reuse.

Customer-facing root-cause summary (one paragraph for post-incident email):
During an automated maintenance restart of our EU inference clusters, a node rejoin race condition caused some nodes to accept requests before internal session caches were fully synchronized. This led to transient failures for requests that depend on warmed session state (for example, long-lived chat sessions or streaming responses). We fixed the reconcile logic, validated the change across the region, and updated routing policies to prevent similar exposure during restarts.

Customer impact details (what customers might observe in logs/metrics):
- Elevated 5xx responses (500/502) and request timeouts between 09:12–09:57 UTC.
- Chat sessions that relied on warm KV cache may return shorter or degraded context in a small subset of requests during the window.
- No persistent data loss; retrying requests succeeded after the window.

Temporary workarounds for customers (recommended immediate actions):
- If you saw increased client-side errors, retry with exponential backoff; our platform will accept retries and route to healthy nodes.
- If you have strict regional affinity requirements and can tolerate small latency increases, enable cross-region failover in the routing policy settings or request CS to enable for your account (temporary handoff).
- For streaming/chat workloads, consider toggling the new "session-tolerant-reconnect" flag (available via API) which prefers re-establishing sessions on stable nodes instead of warming stale pointers. We can enable this per-account if needed.

Planned permanent fixes and timelines (commitments):
- Short-term (1 week): Harden node-rejoin logic with additional invariants and expand canary windows for rolling restarts. (Engineering ticket: INC-9457)
- Medium-term (4–6 weeks): Release a scheduler-level guarantee that nodes will not receive external traffic until ephemeral session state is fully reconciled; will be included in the next runtime minor release.
- Long-term (3 months): Add end-to-end integration tests simulating high-concurrency restarts and extend automatic fallback policies to be route-aware by default.

Customer actionables (what CS/AM teams should do with customers):
- Proactively notify enterprise customers with Dedicated deployments in EU: share this summary and offer to enable cross-region failover for the next 7 days.
- For customers with strict latency/regulatory constraints who cannot failover, offer to schedule a runbook review with solutions-engineering to design a safeguarded maintenance window.
- For any customer that observed degraded output quality, suggest re-running recent eval prompts against the same pinned model version post-incident; offer to run a quick validation sweep (CS will coordinate).

FAQs (short):
Q: Was customer data exposed or deleted?
A: No — we did not observe any data leakage or deletion. The issue affected in-memory session pointers only.
Q: How will you prevent this from recurring?
A: We shipped a hotfix, expanded observability, and have committed to scheduler-level changes and broader testing within the next release cycle.
Q: Can I opt out of automated restarts?
A: Dedicated/Private customers can request maintenance windows or opt for manual restart policies; CS can engage platform-engineering to adjust your settings.

Internal notes / conversation snippets (for context, leave in draft):
- "need to ensure EU canary window increased next maintenance" — SRE channel, 09:45 UTC
- "hotfix looks safe, can we push to eu-central canary now?" — Priya Rao, 09:26 UTC
- Internal ticket: INC-9457 assigned to Priya/Platform, postmortem draft in progress (confluence link above).

Next steps (actions owner and ETA):
- CS: Send tailored notices to top 20 EU customers with Dedicated pools by EOD 2027-07-04 (owner: Alyssa Chen).
- Eng/SRE: Complete scheduler-level change spec and schedule PR for canary deployment by 2027-07-10 (owner: Priya Rao).
- Eng: Add end-to-end restart test scenarios to CI within 8 weeks (owner: Daniel Gomez).

Contact and escalation:
If you need immediate assistance, please contact CS on support@redwood.ai or open a priority ticket referencing INC-9457. For executives/partners, reach out to Marcus Patel (marcus@redwood.ai).

Appendix: Suggested one-paragraph blurb for customer account emails:
On 2027-07-03 an automated cluster restart in our EU region triggered an unexpected state-reconciliation issue that caused transient request failures for around 45 minutes. We deployed a hotfix and adjusted routing to restore availability; no customer data was lost. If you saw errors during this window or want us to enable temporary cross-region failover, reply to this message and we will assist immediately.
